Thousands of “ghost students” use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
raw_text: The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans. In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI. The DOJ seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from “a network associated with Kenyan nationals" after data analysis helped flag likely fraudsters. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division credited new fraud-detection measures implemented by the Trump administration for the arrests. He said that “this is the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya,” while warning fraudsters that the crackdown has only just begun. “If you steal American identities, if you steal taxpayer dollars, if you exploit programs meant to help students build a future—we will find you,” McDonald said. “Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.” Read full article Comments

title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
Analysts find looming launch crisis is "more severe" than anticipated
raw_text: A new report from the analytics firm Quilty Space confirms that, outside of China, the world faces a significant shortage of rockets over the next five years. The firm estimates that between now and 2030, there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches compared to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled. "What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. "What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s." title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
raw_text: General Motors marketed its Smart Driver system as a way for parents to monitor teen drivers or for adults to track their driving behavior. But in 2024, it emerged that GM had been sharing that data with brokers. Those brokers then sold the data to insurance companies , and some drivers found that their insurance became more expensive as a result. To make matters worse, many of those drivers claimed they had no knowledge of ever agreeing to share such data for such purposes. Last year , GM and its OnStar subsidiary entered into a settlement with the FTC, prohibiting them from sharing some kinds of driver data with third parties. The settlement was finalized this January. That agreement banned the two companies from sharing geolocation data or driver behavior data for five years. At the time, GM also discontinued Smart Driver across its entire range. Now the automaker has reached terms with the District of Columbia and 35 states after their attorneys general joined together to sue GM as well. Read full article Comments

title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
raw_text: Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history. The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen. But analysts at Elliptic said the attacker had changed about $3.3 billion into digital assets that could not be frozen and was working to cash those out as traditional currency. title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there's no plug involved
raw_text: Nissan provided flights from Washington, DC, to Santa Barbara, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Rogue Hybrid. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. Nissan has a new version of its bestselling Rogue SUV, and it’s launching the model here with the latest version of its e-Power hybrid system, which Ars tested in February. Most hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid. That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V . Well, mostly; engineers worked out it was more efficient for those cars' gasoline engines to directly drive the wheels at highway speeds, something that to this day makes a certain subset of hybrid car enthusiasts irrationally angry. If you know anyone like that in your life, send them to wherever the nearest Nissan dealership is, because the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is exactly what they’ve been asking for. title: Review: You Can See Everything blurs the view of Elizabeth Holmes' deceit
raw_text: In 2015, biomedical entrepreneur Elizabeth Holmes was Silicon Valley's golden girl, lauded as the youngest and richest self-made female billionaire thanks to the company she founded, Theranos, which was valued at $9 billion at the height of its success. Then it all came crashing down when accusations of fraud surfaced about the company's signature blood-testing device, culminating in a sensational trial. Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison. Holmes is back in the headlines thanks to a new film, You Can See Everything , which depicts the final days before Holmes, having exhausted her appeals , went to prison. Co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim , it's a surreal, absurdist piece that has largely been received with gushing enthusiasm and no small amount of hype, with some declaring it the best film of the year. A few contrarian voices have emerged over the past week with much-needed reality checks, but there's no denying the film is destined to be an awards-season darling. Pardon me for joining the buzzkills, but I cannot in good conscience jump on the You Can See Everything bandwagon. Sure, it has its moments, and the second half is highly entertaining, but there's nothing here to warrant all the breathless hyperbole. For all their much-touted access, Oppenheim and Fielder have produced a surprisingly shallow film that runs in circles, yielding very little fresh or novel insight—into Holmes, personally, or much else. raw_text: Reddit verdwijnt volledig achter een loginmuur. Het sociale netwerk experimenteerde al langer met geforceerde logins. Het gaat om een van de grootste veranderingen van het platform, waarop ook veel gebruikers via Google terechtkwamen als ze bijvoorbeeld technische vragen hadden. Reddit wil met de inlogplicht AI-bots tegenhouden.

title: Techbedrijven VS zoeken geld in Europa, risico voor Europese bedrijven
raw_text: Uit kwartaalcijfers van Amerikaanse techbedrijven deze week blijkt dat ze nog meer geld nodig hebben voor de ontwikkeling van kunstmatige intelligentie (AI). Steeds vaker halen ze dat geld op door leningen uit te geven, eerst in dollars maar nu ook in euro's. Dat brengt ook een risico voor Europese bedrijven met zich mee. Vooral het bouwen van datacenters kost veel geld. Voorheen gebruikten deze hyperscalers , zoals de grote Amerikaanse techbedrijven ook wel genoemd worden, voornamelijk hun eigen winsten, maar dat is niet meer voldoende. Daarom geven ze veel obligaties uit. Dat zijn leningen met rente en een einddatum waarop het totale uitgeleende bedrag terugbetaald wordt. En deze technologiebedrijven doen dat steeds meer in euro's in plaats van dollars. Zo kunnen ze een nieuwe groep beleggers bereiken. Alphabet, het moederbedrijf van Google, was vorig jaar de eerste hyperscaler en gaf twee leningen uit die samen neerkwamen op meer dan 13 miljard euro, en dit jaar nog eens 9 miljard euro. En dit jaar volgde ook Amazon met de grootste bedrijfsobligatie ooit in euro's uitgegeven: 14,5 miljard euro. Dat was reden voor de Europese Centrale Bank om deze ontwikkeling nauw in de gaten te houden. title: De EU Kids Act
raw_text: Deze week praten we met Lotje over de EU Kids Act. Evelyn vertelt over de Time Zone Database. Time Zone Database De PHP-lekken die onlangs plaatsvonden deden Evelyn denken aan de Time Zone Database . In de podcast zegt ze hierover: "Het is een veelgehoord probleem dat het internet een beetje aan elkaar hangt van plakband en vrijwilligers. Hele vitale stukken van onze digitale infrastructuur zijn als hobbyproject begonnen en worden nog steeds vaak door één of een paar developers onderhouden." De EU Kids Act Het gaat de laatste tijd vaak over kinderen en jongeren en het internet. Aan talkshowtafels en in de krant vinden veel mensen dat er een leeftijdsgrens moet komen voor het gebruik van bijvoorbeeld sociale media. Ook in Europa houden jongeren de gemoederen bezig. Er komt een nieuwe wet aan, de EU Kids Act, die kinderen en jongeren online moet beschermen. Deze wet bevat leeftijdsgrenzen voor sociale media die in de gehele Europese Unie moeten gelden. "Helemaal niemand wordt blij van de sociale media van Big Tech zoals die er nu uitzien," aldus Lotje. De problemen zijn bekend: slapeloosheid, verlies van focus, tieners die depressief worden van Instagram, mensen die verslaafd raken aan sociale media, zoals ook in de rechtszaken in de Verenigde Staten naar voren kwam. Het is dus goed dat Europa Big Tech en platformen aan banden wil leggen. Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
raw_text: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding: Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world. Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users. Read full article Comments
